news.title: USPS to upgrade 16 sites just before peak season rush
news.summary: The Postal Service is reworking 16 processing facilities, including sites in Los Angeles and Louisville, with the upgrades slated to wrap up around Thanksgiving.
news.why: Shippers leaning on USPS for holiday parcels should watch transit times out of the affected hubs and keep a backup carrier ready for the first peak weeks.

news.title: FedEx, UPS' upcoming rate hikes: What shippers should know
news.summary: Both major U.S. parcel carriers are taking a 5.9% average general rate increase, but analysts warn that surcharge and pricing-structure changes will push many shippers' real costs higher.
news.why: Run your own shipment profile against the new tariffs and surcharges rather than budgeting to the 5.9% headline, and use the gap as leverage in contract talks.

news.title: Procter & Gamble plans supply chain workforce cuts as automation expands
news.summary: P&G expects automation to let it shrink its product-supply workforce by as much as 30% by 2030.
news.why: Large CPG buyers are betting on automated plants for cost control, so suppliers and co-packers should expect tougher price and data-integration demands from them.

news.title: Under Armour continues efforts to trim SKUs, lead times
news.summary: After cutting its product count by a quarter this year, Under Armour now wants to halve its assortment and focus spending on its best sellers.
news.why: Apparel factories serving brands like this should prepare for fewer but larger orders and push for longer-term volume commitments on the surviving styles.

news.title: Amazon enlists customers in fight against NYC delivery worker bill
news.summary: Amazon is urging New York City shoppers to oppose the proposed Delivery Protection Act, claiming it could add up to $5 to each order.
news.why: Sellers with heavy NYC volume should model higher last-mile costs in case the bill passes, as similar rules could spread to other dense cities.

news.title: Shein to Pay $100M to Settle U.S. Shipping, Customer Service Claims
news.summary: Shein will pay $100 million, without admitting liability, to resolve FTC allegations about misleading delivery times, filtered reviews and unsupported sourcing and cotton-origin claims.
news.why: Any brand making delivery-speed or origin claims should be able to document them, because regulators are now treating supply-chain marketing as enforceable.

news.title: Retailers Face Rising AI Cyberattack Threat Ahead of Black Friday, Many Uninsured
news.summary: Insurance data shows ransomware against retailers spikes in November, while fewer than half of small and mid-sized retailers carry cyber cover.
news.why: Check that key suppliers, 3PLs and your own order systems have tested backups and incident plans, since a peak-week outage costs far more than the insurance.

news.title: Port of Oakland to Purchase Fleet of Tesla EV Semi-Trucks
news.summary: Oakland plans to bring 300 Tesla electric semis into drayage service, with a first batch before year-end and a WattEV depot able to charge 25 trucks at once.
news.why: Importers using Oakland may see more zero-emission drayage options and should ask truckers whether green-lane pricing or capacity differs from diesel moves.

news.title: Maersk and ONE Eye Landmark Global North-South Shipping Alliance
news.summary: Reports say Maersk and Ocean Network Express are moving toward the first worldwide container alliance focused on north-south trades.
news.why: Shippers on Latin America, Africa and Oceania lanes could see service networks and contract options reshaped, so keep 2027 tenders flexible on carrier mix.

news.title: Four More Ships Attacked as Iran Widens Hormuz Crackdown to Tugboats
news.summary: Another four commercial vessels were hit around the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the count of reported tanker strikes there to ten, with harbor tugs now also targeted.
news.why: Expect energy and Gulf-routed freight to carry higher war-risk premiums and delays, so build buffer stock for anything moving through Gulf ports.

news.title: Swedish Club Urges Ships to Avoid Strait of Hormuz as Security Situation Deteriorates
news.summary: Marine insurer The Swedish Club told owners to skip non-essential Hormuz transits, pointing to attacks, congestion and navigation interference.
news.why: When insurers advise avoidance, carriers tend to add surcharges or reroute, so importers from the Gulf region should confirm cover and routing with forwarders now.

news.title: Used Supertankers Now Cost More Than New Ships as Hormuz War Upends Shipping Markets
news.summary: Conflict with Iran has pushed the value of 15-year-old very large crude carriers above the price of newbuild tankers.
news.why: Tight tanker supply keeps crude freight, and by extension fuel and resin input costs, elevated, which buyers should factor into 2027 price negotiations.

news.title: Cargo thieves increase plots to steal shipments over Thanksgiving holiday
news.summary: Verisk CargoNet warns of a jump in carrier-identity fraud during Thanksgiving week, with most incidents clustered around the holiday and in California, Illinois and Texas.
news.why: Vet new carriers carefully this week, avoid leaving loaded trailers unattended over the holiday and treat high-value electronics as prime targets.

news.title: OPEC+ Faces Its Most Consequential Supply Decision of the Year
news.summary: OPEC+ ministers meet at the end of November to decide crude output levels, a call seen as the group's most important of the year.
news.why: The outcome will steer diesel and bunker prices into early 2027, so time fuel-indexed contracts and surcharge reviews around the decision.
